chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) judged regarding the one with a share who forgave, so his forgiveness is allowed; and he judged regarding four brothers, one of them forgave, he said: 'He would be given the wergild, and from the remaining ones, (the wergild) would be raised from them by the share of the one who forgave'.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.عَفْوٌ: Forgiveness (of the right to claim blood money)

ai.seo_question: How is blood money distributed when one heir forgives the killer in Islamic inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudence of *diyah* (blood money) when multiple heirs of the victim are involved, specifically addressing the scenario where one heir forgives the killer while others seek retaliation or compensation. Imam Ali (peace be upon him) rules that the forgiveness of one heir is valid and proportionally reduces the liability of the remaining heirs, ensuring that the killer is not burdened with the full *diyah* for the share that has been waived. This ruling underscores the Shia legal principle that each heir holds an independent right to their portion of the compensation, allowing for partial forgiveness without invalidating the claims of the others.
